title: Canonical projective-line tower maps on etale-origin domains
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and a scheme $S$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. Put $B_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$ and $A_T=((B_n)_T)_n$, with quotient transitions, for schemes $T$ over $S$. Use the coefficient towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers] and their ordinary derived categories [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Let $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ be comparison, and let $\mathscr C^+(T)$ be the full subcategory of $D^+(\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E))$ whose every level has an etale-origin witness [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], meaning it is isomorphic to $\nu_T^*L_n$ for some $L_n\in D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},B_n)$. Put $P=\mathbf P^1_S$, $W=P\times_SP$, $q:P\to S$, $p_1,p_2:W\to P$, and let $\Delta:P\hookrightarrow W$ be the diagonal [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Use the Tate twist, supported diagonal map $\delta_\bullet:\Delta_*A_P\to A_W(1)[2]$, and splitting traces $t_q,t_1,t_2$ of [det-sp-tower-classes]; here $t_i$ is the trace for $p_i$. Write $F=Rq_{*,\bullet}$ and $G=q_\bullet^*(-)(1)[2]$.
The functors $F:\mathscr C^+(P)\to\mathscr C^+(S)$ and $G:\mathscr C^+(S)\to\mathscr C^+(P)$ are well-defined. Each of $q,p_1,p_2,\Delta$ is proper and quasi-compact and quasi-separated; the complementary open of the Cartier divisor $\Delta$ is quasi-compact, and $\Delta_{*,\bullet}$ is exact, so $R\Delta_{*,\bullet}=\Delta_{*,\bullet}$.
For $K\in\mathscr C^+(S)$, $M\in\mathscr C^+(P)$ and $i=1,2$, the canonical projection comparisons
$$K\otimes^LRq_{*,\bullet}(A_P(1)[2])\longrightarrow FGK,$$
$$\Delta_*A_P\otimes^Lp_i^*M\longrightarrow R\Delta_{*,\bullet}M,$$
$$M\otimes^LRp_{i*,\bullet}(A_W(1)[2])\longrightarrow Rp_{i*,\bullet}(p_i^*M(1)[2])$$
and the proper exchange $q_\bullet^*FM\to Rp_{2*,\bullet}p_1^*M$ (also with the two projections exchanged) are isomorphisms. All their source and target objects are bounded below. The section-model tensor, direct-image composition and comparison maps [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] identify their level-$n$ evaluations with the corresponding ordinary etale maps after $\nu^*$ and the canonical direct-image mate comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. This asserts compatibility of the specified maps, not just existence of isomorphic objects.
Write $\eta_M$ for the composite
$$M\simeq Rp_{2*,\bullet}\Delta_*M\simeq Rp_{2*,\bullet}(\Delta_*A_P\otimes^Lp_1^*M)\xrightarrow{Rp_{2*,\bullet}(\delta_\bullet\otimes1)}Rp_{2*,\bullet}(p_1^*M)(1)[2]\simeq GFM,$$
and $\varepsilon_K$ for
$$FGK\simeq K\otimes^LRq_{*,\bullet}(A_P(1)[2])\xrightarrow{1\otimes t_q}K,$$
where composition, projection and exchange are the canonical mate maps on the ringed topos of towers [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections].
These formulas define natural transformations $\eta:1\to GF$ and $\varepsilon:FG\to1$ on the displayed domains. Their level-$n$ evaluations are exactly the diagonal-defined and splitting-trace-defined finite formulas with coefficient ring $B_n$, transported by $\nu^*$. This compatibility includes the composition source identification for $p_i\Delta=1_P$, twists and shifts. No finite-Tor assumption on $K$ or $M$ is required.

proof.text: The projective-space properness theorem makes $q$ proper; $p_1,p_2$ are its base changes, hence proper. Proper means separated and finite type; finite type includes quasi-compactness, and a separated morphism is quasi-separated. The diagonal of the separated map $q$ is closed, so $\Delta$ is proper too and has the same qcqs consequences. Its Cartier property is supplied by the diagonal-ideal lemma. To check the complementary open is quasi-compact as an immersion, work over an affine base open and use the four standard affine product charts. The diagonal equations are $t-u$, $tv-1$, $su-1$, $s-v$ on the finite/finite, finite/infinite, infinite/finite, infinite/infinite charts. The complement on each chart is the corresponding principal open. Each is affine, hence quasi-compact; this is a cover-local check on the target, requiring no quasi-compactness of $S$.

source.place: Construction: geometry of the two projections and the diagonal; four-chart verification of the quasi-compact complementary open

proof.text: Apply exactness of pro-etale closed direct image with quasi-compact complementary open to $\Delta$, separately with each constant finite ring $B_n$. Kernels and cokernels in the varying-ring tower category are componentwise, so $\Delta_{*,\bullet}$ is exact. Its termwise complex functor therefore computes its derived functor on bounded-below complexes: an exact functor takes acyclic complexes to acyclic complexes, so its localization agrees with its right derived functor. Thus $R\Delta_{*,\bullet}=\Delta_{*,\bullet}$ canonically, and it preserves every lower bound.

source.place: Tag 09A9, lemma-closed-immersion-complement-retrocompact-exact; passage to towers by componentwise exactness

proof.text: Use the simultaneous section-model operations to form the tensor, projection transposes, exchange and composition maps in the ordinary unbounded tower derived categories. Evaluation preserves these specified words, including their units and counits. The compatible-root cover trivializes the Tate line tower simultaneously at all levels. Tensor by this line is exact, since it becomes tensor by the ring on that cover, and is invertible with inverse the negative twist. The line is locally free of rank one as a module in the inverse-system topos, hence perfect there. The perfect ringed-site projection theorem, applied with this line on the target of $q$ or $p_i$, gives the canonical isomorphisms $Rh_*(C(1)[2])\simeq(Rh_*C)(1)[2]$. This also fixes the twist identifications in the trace and in the displayed formulas.

source.place: Construction and Levels: ordinary tower operations and twists; perfect coefficient line projection (Stacks 0944)

proof.text: For $h=q,p_1,p_2$, use the splitting of the tower classes lemma over the base of $h$, then the twist identification of Step 3. It gives $Rh_{*,\bullet}(A(1)[2])\simeq A(1)[2]\oplus A$. If $K$ or $M$ has cohomology zero below $a$, its tensor with this object has zero cohomology below $a-2$: tensor distributes over the two summands and tensor by either line is exact. Exact inverse images, closed direct image, and twists preserve lower bounds, the shift $[2]$ lowers them by two, and right derived direct image preserves lower bounds. The latter assertion follows by taking the bounded-below injective resolution of a complex zero below that bound. Consequently all the projection sources involving $q$ or $p_i$, their targets, and the exchange sources and targets have uniform lower bounds. The remaining supported projection source is checked in Step 7.

source.place: Construction: splitting traces and domains of the projection maps

proof.text:
Fix a level $n$ and retain an origin witness $
u_P^*L_n\simeq M_n$. The tower direct-image evaluation followed by the canonical direct-image mate gives $(FM)_n\simeq Rq_{p,*}
u_P^*L_n\simeq
u_S^*Rq_{e,*}L_n$, a bounded-below etale origin. For a witness $
u_S^*H_n\simeq K_n$, exact pullback comparison, the monoidal comparison $
u_P^*(U\otimes^LV)\simeq
u_P^*U\otimes^L
u_P^*V$ of the comparison morphism with constant rings, and the root-site isomorphism $\sigma:
u_P^*B_{n,P}(1)_{\mathrm{et}}\simeq B_{n,P}(1)$ give $(GK)_n\simeq
u_P^*(q_e^{-1}H_n(1)[2])$. The pro-etale twist here is the root tower of the tower classes, whose level $n$ is the pro-etale root tensor $D_{\ell^n,P}$ of the root-site comparison. Steps 3-4 give the uniform tower bounds, so these witnesses prove that $F$ and $G$ restrict to the displayed full subcategories. The same argument applies to $p_i$ and $\Delta$ whenever used below. There is no need to choose the $L_n$ or $H_n$ compatibly with tower transitions.

source.place: Levels: direct-image and inverse-image comparison on bounded-below origin witnesses

proof.text:
For a qcqs map $h:U	o V$ apply the ringed exchange/tensor coherence theorem to the commutative square with vertical maps $h_e,h_p$ and horizontal comparison maps $
u_U,
u_V$. This is a square of ringed topoi with the constant rings $B_n$; cartesianness is not needed. Its exchange is exactly $b_h:
u_V^*Rh_{e,*}	o Rh_{p,*}
u_U^*$, because both are the transpose of the pullback comparison followed by the etale counit. The theorem therefore identifies the specified projection maps, under the monoidal tensor and pullback comparisons, by
$$b_{h,E\otimes h_e^*Q}\,
u_V^*(\pi^e_{h,E,Q})=\pi^p_{h,
u_U^*E,
u_V^*Q}(b_{h,E}\otimes1).$$
Here the target also uses $
u_U^*h_e^*Q\simeq h_p^*
u_V^*Q$. The comparisons $b$ are used only for bounded-below $E$ and $E\otimes h_e^*Q$, as verified in Step 7. Naturality carries the equality through any specified origin witnesses, without asserting that a tower of witnesses exists.

source.place: Tag 0E48, remark-compatible-with-diagram, applied to etale/pro-etale comparison; Tag 07A4 tensor comparison

proof.text: At level $n$ apply the finite-ring ordinary-etale proper projection theorem to $(h,E,Q)=(q,B_{n,P}(1)[2],H_n)$, to $(p_i,B_{n,W}(1)[2],L_n)$, and to $(\Delta,B_{n,P},p_{i,e}^*L_n)$. All three maps are isomorphisms without a Tor hypothesis. In the first two cases $E\otimes h_e^*Q$ is a shifted line twist of an exact inverse image, so is bounded below. In the third it is $L_n$, using $p_i\Delta=1_P$, so again is bounded below. Step 6 transports these particular maps to the pro-etale site; Step 3 identifies them with the evaluations of the actual tower maps. Joint conservativity of derived evaluations makes each tower projection invertible. Moreover the supported source $\Delta_*A_P\otimes^Lp_i^*M$ has the same lower bound as $\Delta_*M$: the evaluated isomorphisms identify their cohomology, and exact componentwise evaluations detect vanishing of each cohomology tower. This completes the boundedness assertion without using finite Tor amplitude of $K$ or $M$.

source.place: Tag 0F0G, lemma-projection-formula-proper-mod-n; specialize to the three displayed proper maps

proof.text: The square with $q,q$ and $p_1,p_2$ is Cartesian. At level $n$, the exchange-transport theorem identifies its specified ordinary-etale exchange with its specified pro-etale mate under the canonical direct-image and pullback comparisons. Ordinary-etale proper base change over the torsion ring $B_n$ makes this exchange invertible on $L_n$. Evaluation of the tower exchange is precisely this mate by the section-model theorem. Joint conservativity therefore makes $q_\bullet^*FM\to Rp_{2*,\bullet}p_1^*M$ invertible. Swapping the two factors gives the other exchange; the same proof applies with $p_1$ and $p_2$ interchanged.

source.place: Construction: Cartesian projective-line square; Tag 0DDE, lemma-proper-base-change-mod-n

proof.text: Use the canonical direct-image compositor for $p_i\Delta=1_P$ to identify $M$ with $Rp_{i*,\bullet}\Delta_*M$, using Step 2. This identification evaluates to the finite compositor. It also agrees with transport by $\nu^*$: the pullback comparisons $a$ respect identities and composites, so the pullback square for $p_i\Delta$ is the pasting of those for $\Delta$ and $p_i$; the two direct-image comparisons are the mates of this pasted pullback square, so the mate-pasting identity identifies their composite with the comparison for the composite map. The identity clause makes the comparison for $1_P$ the identity. The monoidal and adjunction-compatible composition theorem gives the corresponding compatibility with tensor, symmetry and the identity pullback. The shift comparisons in the ringed projection theorem fix the integer shifts as well. Hence these are the specified composition source, twist and shift identifications used in $\eta$, not independently chosen isomorphisms of their objects.

source.place: Levels: source composition identification for the diagonal unit; Tags 0D6E and 0B65 for composition and mates

proof.text:
Now compose the inverse projection and exchange isomorphisms proved in Steps 7-8 with $Rp_{2*, ullet}(\delta_ ullet\otimes1)$, as written in the statement, to define $\eta_M$. Compose the inverse $q$-projection with $1\otimes t_q$ to define $\varepsilon_K$. The comparisons are natural, and inversion of a natural isomorphism is natural (multiply its naturality square by its two inverses), so the composites are natural transformations. Evaluation sends $\delta_ ullet$ and $t_q$ to the finite supported diagonal class and splitting trace by the tower classes lemma. The supported Cartier comparison identifies that class, including its source and positive Kummer sign, with the ordinary-etale class after $
u^*$. For the trace, the evaluated $t_q$ is $\operatorname{pr}_2$ of the inverse of the finite unit/Chern splitting whose Chern component is the pulled-back etale Kummer class of $\mathcal O_P(1)$, with the pro-etale root twist. The counit normalization of the direct-image comparison $b_q$, transposed, shows that $b_q\circ
u_S^*$ carries the etale unit to the pro-etale unit and the etale adjoint of the Chern class to the pro-etale adjoint of its pullback; with $\sigma$ on the twist, $b_q$ therefore carries $
u_S^*$ of the etale splitting to the evaluated tower splitting, hence $
u_S^*$ of the etale trace to the evaluated $t_q$. The same holds for $t_1,t_2$ over $P$. Steps 6, 8 and 9 identify every remaining projection, exchange and composition arrow, including inverse arrows. Thus the evaluated composites are exactly the asserted ordinary-etale diagonal and splitting-trace formulas after comparison. The verification concerns these composites of specified maps, and imposes no finite-Tor or normalization condition.
